description: we are building the most apt and the best simulator and training rig for aspiring astronauts or the ones who are in the basic training which will help them gain expertise in a shorter time
summary: OUTPOST is a browser-based mission game for young astronauts. The player chooses a vehicle and launch parameters before flying to the Moon or Mars and landing cargo on their outpost. The player will have to manage resources (power, water, oxygen) over 2 simulated days. The choices made by the player will lead to calculated outcomes, including some failures. As NASA historical observations are used, assumptions are clear to see and there is human-led support. This means learners can see why certain choices have been made when comparing outcomes. Optionally there is a pilot for a precision landing that shows machine learning. OUTPOST is an educational prototype and does not provide any actual astronaut certification or mission planning.
details:
OUTPOST allows the junior astronaut to make decisions, view the outcome of their decisions and learn from them. The learner will navigate their way to either the Moon or Mars from Earth. Once launched they will then manage the outpost.

This involves adjusting the launch settings, this includes the spacecraft, payload, wind, launch window, throttle and much more. They can ask for an estimate, make adjustments and then press play to see the rocket go through the 3D scene. If they fail at launch they can then make adjustments and try again.

They will need to balance between landing and fuel usage. Then once they reach the outpost they will need to manage power, water and oxygen for 48 hours. They can make comparisons between similar decision points and see how one aspect can affect another. For example, producing oxygen can impact water and energy. Goals to achieve, feedback and reflection allows them to understand the outcome of their decisions.

The optional AI pilot during landing allows them to experiment further. The model has been trained using machine learning with examples from a simulated controller. This means the throttle can be calculated based on the state of landing. They can watch how it performs compared to doing it manually. They can pause or override the model. Tips are given based on the situation; fuel warning. These have been programmed using rules.

OUTPOST has been created using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The JavaScript handles the controls, calculations and mission. Three.js has been used to create the interactive 3D scenes. The landing model uses supervised imitation learning with linear regression.

References to NASA have been used to give initial values and context. This includes data about the Moon and Mars, forces on the rocket and historical data about space weather and radiation. OUTPOST puts this into an educational simulation so they can experiment, compare and make
